chains.title: No TF-mediated allelic effect of rs56007086; association may be linked or passenger
predictions: No reproducible allele-specific TF ChIP or enhancer-reporter difference at this base.
Any breast cancer association at 16q12 is driven by a linked variant or haplotype context, not by rs56007086 itself.
The variant may be a passenger in a regulatory hotspot without a direct allele-specific TF effect.
falsified_if: A robust allele-specific TF occupancy or enhancer activity difference is demonstrated at this base.
CRISPR editing of rs56007086 alone changes TOX3 expression or a breast cancer-relevant phenotype.
Fine-mapping shows this base, rather than a linked variant, is the functional allele.

chains.title: Ref allele preserves a stronger SPDEF site in the TOX3 enhancer; alt allele weakens SPDEF binding

links.claim: SPDEF binds the ref G allele more strongly than the alt A allele. SPDEF has an ENCODE ChIP-seq peak over the variant in MCF-7 and is well expressed in MCF7. Its own QBiC-SELEX model detects a ref-gain effect (z -7.0, effect -0.244), with the ref site at the 99.7th percentile versus 95.0th for alt. This is the only chain here with an own-model QBiC-SELEX result plus matching MCF-7 occupancy.

The variant lies in the VEP-annotated ENSR16_9QTBS enhancer. No cCRE overlaps the base itself; the nearest dELS is 38 bp away and has active enhancer marks (H3K27ac z 6.1, DNase z 4.2). The element shows extensive TF ChIP-seq occupancy, consistent with an active regulatory element, but the cCRE assignment is nearby rather than base-overlapping.

TOX3 is the nearest protein-coding gene (17.6 kb upstream) and is a breast-cancer-associated locus by Open Targets (overall score 0.58; genetic_association 0.91, literature 0.89). However, there is no GTEx eQTL and no breast eQTL/ASE evidence for this SNP, so the SNP-to-TOX3 link remains inferential.
MCF7 is a relevant breast cancer epithelial context: SPDEF is expressed in DepMap MCF7 at 72.51 TPM (rank 40/1626) and has an ENCODE ChIP-seq peak over the variant in MCF-7.

TOX3 is linked to breast cancer in Open Targets and locus literature, but the supplied evidence does not establish that this base changes TOX3 expression or disease risk. If SPDEF activates the enhancer, loss of SPDEF binding on alt would lower TOX3; if SPDEF represses, alt would increase TOX3. The downstream sign is unresolved.

predictions: Allele-specific SPDEF ChIP will show higher ref G occupancy than alt A at rs56007086.
SPDEF knockdown or overexpression will alter the allelic enhancer activity of the ENSR16_9QTBS/dELS element in MCF7.
The allele-dependent enhancer effect should be SPDEF-dependent and not require TCF7L2.
falsified_if: SPDEF ChIP is not allele-specific at this base.
The SPDEF ref-gain QBiC-SELEX result does not reproduce in an allele-specific reporter or direct binding assay.
SPDEF perturbation does not alter TOX3 enhancer activity or TOX3 expression.

chains.title: Alt allele creates a stronger TCF7L2 site in the TOX3 enhancer

links.claim: TCF7L2 binds the alt A allele more strongly in the QBiC-SELEX assay (z 12.52, effect 0.745; alt site rises from the 57.0th to 97.8th percentile), and TCF7L2 has an ENCODE ChIP-seq peak over the variant in MCF-7. The evidence is weakened because TCF7L2 has no own QBiC-SELEX model; the best model is CIS-BP-mapped from TCF7L1, and TCF7L2 is expressed at only 4.89 TPM in MCF7.

The variant lies in the VEP-annotated ENSR16_9QTBS enhancer. No cCRE overlaps the base; the nearest dELS is 38 bp away and has active enhancer marks and extensive TF ChIP-seq occupancy. The element assignment is therefore nearby-enhancer rather than base-overlapping.

TOX3 is the nearest protein-coding gene and is a breast-cancer-associated locus in Open Targets. No GTEx eQTL and no breast eQTL/ASE support this SNP as a direct TOX3 regulatory variant, so the target-gene link is inferential.

MCF7 is a relevant breast cancer context and has TCF7L2 ChIP-seq occupancy over the variant. However, TCF7L2 expression is low in MCF7 (4.89 TPM, rank 642/1626), weakening it as the primary allele-specific TF.

TOX3 is linked to breast cancer, but the supplied evidence does not establish that this variant alters TOX3 expression or disease risk. If TCF7L2 activates the enhancer, the alt allele would increase TOX3; if TCF7L2 represses, the direction would reverse. The downstream sign is unresolved.

next_experiment: The cheapest experiment that separates the top two chains is allele-specific SPDEF ChIP-qPCR/ddPCR at rs56007086 in a heterozygous breast cancer line (MCF7 if heterozygous; otherwise a heterozygous patient-derived line). The SPDEF chain predicts ref G > alt A SPDEF occupancy, whereas the null predicts no reproducible allele-specific SPDEF occupancy. This is cheaper than enhancer-reporter or CRISPR editing and directly tests the best-supported TF allele effect.

Candidates are TFs whose ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant and that are expressed (DepMap line ACH-000019), bound here before bound elsewhere, then by |z|; then expressed TFs ENCODE never assayed whose best model passes the gate (occupancy unknown). Shown: 10 of 79 occupied, 5 of 137 with unknown occupancy. Left out: 49 TFs assayed in the matching biosample and 425 assayed only elsewhere, none with a peak here; 20 bound but below 1 TPM.
